ScaleSight works with the data and planning context you already have. We investigate what changed, compare the available options, and bring your team a reviewed recommendation. The workspace supports the service; your team does not have another planning tool to operate.
Talk through a planning decision
Start with the commitment, then agree the inputs.
01 Choose the decision
Agree the upcoming buy, production, replenishment or allocation decision, the products and channels involved, the timing and the decision owner.
02 Agree the inputs
Start with relevant sales or sell-through, stock, open purchase orders, lead times and product definitions. Add returns, exchanges, promotions, costs or retailer data where the question needs them.
03 Investigate the signal
Check availability, promotions, seasonality, launches and channel changes. Use statistical or machine-learning methods where useful, with assumptions and limits visible.
04 Compare the options
Compare practical choices on quantity, timing or mix against supply constraints, service risk and cash exposure.
05 Review and recommend
Apply planning review and prepare a concise recommendation for your team to discuss and decide.
06 Maintain the work
Refresh the agreed analysis during the engagement and revisit the decisions when the evidence or constraints change.
Forecasts create evidence. Planning review gives it context.
A demand estimate is one input. We also examine what is available, what is already committed, what can arrive in time and what each option requires from cash and capacity.
See an illustrative planning brief
Use the data that answers the question.
Demand
Sales and sell-through at the useful product, channel and time level. Separate opening orders from repeat demand where the data allows.
Stock and incoming supply
Available and committed stock, open purchase orders, arrival dates and relevant transfer constraints.
Operating constraints
Lead times, minimum order quantities, production slots, pack sizes and shelf life where relevant.
Commercial context
Promotions, launches, costs, returns or exchanges when they materially change the decision.
We agree the data sources and access method during scoping. The analysis reflects the coverage and quality of the available inputs.
A clear recommendation, with a clear owner.

ScaleSight maintains the agreed analysis, investigates exceptions, compares options and prepares the reviewed brief. Your team supplies operating context, validates constraints, chooses the action and executes through its own processes.
Can you work alongside our planning system?
Yes. We scope the additional analysis around your existing process and the decision that needs attention.
Is every engagement machine learning?
No. The question, data and decision horizon determine which methods are useful.
What if the data is incomplete?
We identify the gaps, state the assumptions and agree whether a narrower investigation can still be useful.
Will you place orders for us?
Your team retains approval and execution of buys, production and allocation.
Have an upcoming inventory decision?
Talk it through with us.
30-DAY FOCUSED PLANNING PILOT
Test the managed planning approach on one real decision.

Choose one upcoming buy, production run or allocation decision. ScaleSight uses agreed inputs to investigate the signal, compare options and bring reviewed recommendations. At the end, decide whether ongoing review is useful enough to make recurring.
Talk through a planning decision
A useful starting point has a real commitment attached.

A strong pilot has a named decision owner, an upcoming commitment date, relevant data and a choice that remains open. It can support a lean team or add bandwidth around an established planning process.
An upcoming production run with competing flavor signals.
A buying decision affected by size-level returns or availability.
A supply delay that changes allocation or promotion choices.
Four weeks, one agreed decision scope.
1 / Scope
Agree the decision, products, channels, owner, timing, inputs and constraints. Define how usefulness will be judged. Establish the first decision note and data-gap log.
2 / Establish the read
Prepare and check inputs, distinguish demand from availability effects, and document the baseline and assumptions. Review the first evidence-led read.
3 / Compare options
Investigate the change and compare feasible quantity, timing or mix choices against supply, service and cash constraints.
4 / Review and choose
Review the recommendation, remaining uncertainty and learning. Agree whether to stop, refine the scope or continue with recurring support.
What the pilot gives your team
A decision-specific workspace
A shared view of the evidence, assumptions and alternatives for the agreed question.
Maintained analysis
Forecasts, demand checks and scenarios appropriate to the available data and decision.
Reviewed decision briefs
What changed, what we checked, the options, the recommended action and the cash and service implications.
A final review
A record of the findings, outstanding questions and whether continued support would be useful.
Who does what
ScaleSight
Your team
Frame the analytical question and organize agreed inputs.
Provide relevant data and explain operating constraints.
Investigate signals, compare options and document assumptions.
Validate lead times, costs, MOQs, commitments and practical feasibility.
Prepare and review recommendations within scope.
Review the trade-offs, make final decisions and execute.
Judge the pilot by the decision it supports.

Did the analysis clarify the choice? Did it arrive before the commitment? Were the assumptions and trade-offs usable? Did it help the team decide what to change, hold or investigate? We quantify effects where the data supports them.
Continue when the review earns its place.

After the pilot, we review what was useful and what remains open. Any ongoing engagement has an agreed decision scope, review cadence and fee. Continued access and support are defined in that agreement.
How long is the pilot?
The proposed pilot is 30 days. We agree the start date, decision deadline and data readiness before work begins.
What does it cost?
We confirm the fee after agreeing the decision, data requirements and review scope.
How much time will our team need?
We agree the onboarding and review time during scoping, based on the data and operating context.
Do we need Shopify?
No single sales platform defines fit. We first confirm whether the relevant data can support the question.
Do you replace our planner or analyst?
ScaleSight adds analytical planning capacity around an agreed scope. Your team retains operational ownership.
Do you guarantee savings or fewer stockouts?
We assess evidence and trade-offs. Business outcomes depend on demand, data quality, constraints and the decisions your team takes.
What happens if the data cannot support the question?
We review the limitation with you and agree whether to narrow the question or change the approach.
What happens after 30 days?
We review the work together. Continued analysis, support and workspace access require an agreed next scope.

What a reviewed planning brief can contain
When supply timing changes, what should happen to the promotion?
CPG / supply timing
Evidence to examine: available stock, committed orders, revised arrival dates and expected promotion demand.
Options to compare: expedite eligible supply, split the receipt, reallocate usable stock or adjust the promotion.
Decision output: a timing recommendation with cash, service and feasibility trade-offs.
Open illustrative workspace
Is the launch adding demand or shifting the flavor mix?
Food / launch demand
Evidence to examine: total portfolio sales, availability, opening fill, repeat orders and shared production capacity.
Options to compare: increase total output, change the mix within the planned run or hold until repeat demand is clearer.
Decision output: a next-run recommendation with component, capacity and cash implications.
Open illustrative workspace
Which size demand should shape the next buy?
Apparel / size depth
Evidence to examine: sales by size, in-stock exposure, returns, exchanges and retained demand.
Options to compare: deepen selected sizes, rebalance the size curve or hold depth pending better evidence.
Decision output: a size-depth recommendation with lead-time, stock and cash trade-offs.

Bring us a planning question.
Talk through a planning decision
Better questions. Clearer commitments.
I started ScaleSight to make deeper planning analysis useful before a brand commits more cash.
I’m Arman, a data scientist. In consumer brands, a forecast is only one input to a much larger decision: what to buy or produce, how much, when, and what the choice means for cash and availability.

ScaleSight brings data-science analysis and supply-chain review together around the commitments a brand has to make. We work from agreed sales, inventory, incoming supply and lead-time data, investigate changing demand, and compare the options. We maintain the analysis and bring the team a clear recommendation; the team keeps the final call.

Larger brands often hire planners, analysts and data-science specialists around their systems. ScaleSight gives growing brands access to analytical support without building every capability internally. For lean teams, that adds planning capability. For established teams, it adds bandwidth around a defined investigation.

Keep ownership with the client.

sampleBrief.context: Synthetic beverage example. Next production slot: 12 November. Decision owner: Brand operations.

fields.label: What changed
fields.value: Flavor A sold 1,200 units over four weeks; B sold 800. B was unavailable for six days.

fields.label: What we checked
fields.value: Total sales, availability, repeat orders, incoming supply and shared run capacity. A faster observed rate alone does not establish incremental demand.

fields.label: Recommended action
fields.value: Investigate B availability before increasing total volume. Compare an unchanged total run with a revised mix.

fields.label: Quantity and timing
fields.value: Compare 6,000 units at 3,000 A / 3,000 B with 3,600 A / 2,400 B before the next slot is committed.

fields.label: Cash and service trade-off
fields.value: At an assumed $2 unit cost, both total $12,000 in product cost. Timing, packaging, freight and lost-sales risk still require review.

fields.label: Assumptions and next signal
fields.value: Synthetic figures; equal unit costs assumed. Recheck B after seven in-stock days and validate MOQ, committed stock and lead time.
